verified_facts: DAF solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006, 'RFLP Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base, and Clear Space Force Station.' Proposals due June 29, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT.
Offerors may propose for any subset of the three locations.
News-Miner (June 11): three proposed Eielson sites and one Clear SFS parcel would draw power from GVEA's grid; GVEA recommended connection to its 138-kV line for major loads.
The RFLP notes Southcentral Alaska is experiencing a mounting natural gas shortage as Cook Inlet reserves dwindle (quoted via Alaska's News Source June 8/12).

Sarah Hollister, Fairbanks-area resident, verbatim in News-Miner: 'This will be on the backs of GVEA members.' Also: 'These are for-profit companies looking to lease military lands that don't live here.'

Robert Moriarty, Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Installations, News-Miner: 'By making this land available, we are supporting the growing demands of the AI industry while generating value that directly supports our missions.'
HB 381 passed the Alaska House 34-5 on June 12, 2026 (APM, ADN).
It replaces a 2% statewide oil-and-gas property tax with a per-unit volumetric tax on gas through the Alaska LNG pipeline, an 80-90% reduction vs current law (APM).
ADN (June 18): without the break the state and municipalities would get roughly $850 million more per year. Total state revenue with the break ~$23B through 2062 (APM).
Senate majority caucus 'rule of 11' requires 11 of 14 members to advance a bill to the floor; as of June 18 the Senate had not voted, bill stalled in Senate Finance (ADN, APM).
Special session 30-day clock expires midnight Friday June 19, 2026. Dunleavy vetoed 9 bills June 18 and threatened a second special session (ADN, APM).
Dunleavy (ADN): 'If the Senate does run out of time by Friday midnight, I will issue a call for a second special session.'
ADN: Glenfarne says the bill's terms will help advance Alaska LNG as it looks to lock up deals with gas producers and buyers and secure loans.

FERC voted unanimously on or about June 18, 2026 to require that large-load customers including AI data centers be able to connect to the transmission system in a timely, orderly manner and bear the full cost of grid upgrades needed for their connections (AP wire via ADN).
FERC Chair Laura Swett (AP): 'Many Americans are increasingly concerned about the interconnection of large (power) loads, and data centers will increase their bills.'
Alaska is not part of any FERC RTO/ISO and is not directly subject to the order.
NOAA's 2026 Eastern Bering Sea Bottom Trawl Survey is underway (early June through end of July); NOAA page last updated June 16, 2026.
The F/V Northwest Explorer carries an Imaging FlowCytobot (IFCB), an automated microscope producing real-time images of phytoplankton (NOAA).
NOAA partners with AOOS; the AOOS IFCB program states an algorithm has been developed to automatically flag harmful algal cells (AOOS).
Monitored harmful species include Alexandrium, Pseudo-nitzschia, Dinophysis (NOAA).

Dunleavy vetoed SB 258 on June 18, 2026, described by ADN as 'Cloud services choice preservation,' preserving the state's ability to choose whether to use cloud services for software-based applications. Sponsored by Sen. Jesse Kiehl. Passed Senate unanimously; 26 of 40 House members voted for it.
Dunleavy rationale (ADN): restrictions 'could reduce flexibility, limit access to needed products, and increase costs for agencies and local governments.'

8 Star Alaska (Glenfarne subsidiary) and Alaska building trades councils signed an MOU June 11-12, 2026 prioritizing Alaska workers as the first and primary source of construction labor on Alaska LNG.
~12,000 construction workers anticipated (ADN notes not all from Alaska); up to 1,000 long-term operations roles (Glenfarne). Neither source mentions automation.
Rex Canon, Co-President 8 Star Alaska: 'We are committed to building Alaska LNG with a highly skilled Alaska workforce as the first and primary source of construction labor.'
